title: QA review agent should assess token usage and flag inefficiencies
description: The QA review at run end assesses spec compliance but does not consider whether the run was cost-efficient. Redundant reads, re-reads of the same file, oversized prompts (start_spec is 144K characters), and unnecessary tool calls inflate cost without adding value. The run phase cost breakdown (see companion signal) will provide the data; the QA agent needs to act on it.
proposed_resolution: Extend the QA review prompt to include a cost_efficiency section that runs after compliance checking. Using the phase cost breakdown from the run file, the reviewer must flag: (1) any file read more than once in the same phase without intervening writes, (2) any single prompt component larger than a configurable threshold (default 50K characters), (3) any tool call whose output was not referenced in a subsequent action. Findings are included in the review output with ✓/✗ format and may generate SkillImprovement signals. Depends on run-phase-cost-breakdown.
